tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the Fulcrum projects in this organization, with their ids and clients. Call this when you do not already know which project the work in this repository belongs to — every other project-scoped tool accepts either the id or the name this returns.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Start a new project in Fulcrum, for a client that may or may not exist yet. Use it when the work in this repository has no project to hang off — it is the one step that otherwise means leaving your session and opening the app. Returns the id and short code you need to push cards at it. The client is matched by name and created only if there is no such client already.

work_weeks.description: Rough calendar weeks of delivery, if it is known

complexity_scale.description: Name of an existing scale; defaults to the organization's

short_code.description: 2-6 characters, used in card ids like FUL-17. Generated if omitted.

adopt.description: When a project of this name already exists, use it instead of refusing. Its cards are PROPOSED rather than put on the board — the project is not new, so somebody may already be living with it. Defaults to false.

features.description: Cards to start the project with. These land ON the board, already accepted, whatever your token's direct access — at the instant you are creating the project there is nobody else to review them. Supply concise descriptions only; PRD authoring is a separate explicit step for one feature at a time. Leave it out and the project starts empty.

description.description: What the work is, in markdown.

estimates.description: Rough hours per role, if you know them. Omit rather than guess.

tools.name: find_features
tools.description: Search the execution board for cards. Every filter is optional and they combine; free text searches card names, task titles, descriptions, product requirements and comments. Returns one summary line per card — call get_feature for the full brief on whichever one you mean to work on. Use it to find work, to see what is already in flight, and to check whether something like this has been built before.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name. Omit to search the whole organization.

limit.description: Maximum cards to return (default 50, capped at 200)

tools.name: get_feature
tools.description: Read everything one card asks for: its description, product requirements, estimates by role, task checklist, dependencies in both directions, labels, release, linked branches, approval state and recent comments. Accepts a short id like FUL-17 or a numeric id. This is the tool to call before starting work on a card, and again when you are unsure what it was actually asking for.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: get_feature_prd
tools.description: Read one card's product requirements in full. get_feature already includes them when they are short, and says so when it has truncated them — call this when it did, or when you need to quote the requirements exactly rather than work from a summary.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: get_project_prompt
tools.description: Read the estimation context Fulcrum itself uses for a project: the organization's rubric, its delivery roles, the complexity scale, its releases, and the inventory of features this team has already priced. Read it before sizing anything, so the estimate reflects how this team actually sizes work rather than a generic guess. scope 'estimating' is the bundle a local estimate should follow; 'full' also includes the connected repository facts and the closing guidance. Weekly rates are never included in either — this returns hours, never cost.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: get_project_prompt_without_estimates
tools.description: Read the same estimation context as get_project_prompt — the organization's rubric, its delivery roles, the complexity scale, its releases and the inventory of features — with every feature's estimate withheld. Call it instead of get_project_prompt when you are about to estimate a card and have been asked to do so before seeing its current estimate: the inventory would otherwise show you that estimate, and every other card's, before your own is made. Everything else is identical, and it takes the same arguments.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: get_project_summary
tools.description: Read a project's totals in one call: how many cards are in each column and each priority, the committed hours per role — overall, by priority and by release — what is set aside (won't-haves, proposals still in the Inbox, archived cards), what is waiting on a person to review, and the releases in order. Call it after changing cards to see where the estimate landed, or before, to know what you are working with, instead of reading every card. Hours only — never rates or cost.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: get_schedule
tools.description: Read a project's schedule as its staffing timeline has it: the project window (start, end, weeks) beside where the scheduled work actually ends, so how far it runs past the window or how much slack is left; per role, the committed hours, how many are on the timeline, the weeks that role's work spans and how full its staffing is; each release's start and end; every card that is not on the timeline and why (no estimate, won't have, nobody staffed in its role, waiting on work that is not placed, a loop of dependencies, or no room left in the staffed weeks); and how many Inbox proposals are left out because nobody has accepted them. Call it when someone asks when the work lands, and before and after schedule_project. Hours and dates only — never rates or cost.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: get_estimation_session
tools.description: Read the estimation conversation for a project: what the client has already answered, which questions are still open, which documents are in play, and the recent back-and-forth. Read it before estimating anything that was discussed with a client, so you build on the thread rather than re-asking it. Documents are listed by name, not inlined. The conversation is the recent tail, and says so when there is more.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: add_session_note
tools.description: Leave a note in a project's estimation conversation, so work done outside the app is not invisible to it. Use it when you have estimated or scoped something locally: say what you covered, what you assumed, and what is still open. Write it for the person who opens the thread next week, not as a log — it is a message in a conversation people read, not a transcript.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: add_project_document
tools.description: Hand a project's estimator a reference document — a write-up of what the codebase already does, a spec, notes from a call — so Fulcrum's estimation chat reads it and get_estimation_session lists it, exactly as if a person had uploaded it to the session's files. Use it for material the estimate should rest on that is too long for a note. Content is markdown and can be long: up to 10 MB is stored, an upload's ceiling, and a larger document is refused once it arrives, so split one that big. It is in the estimator's context unless you say otherwise. Calling it again with the same title replaces that document's content instead of adding a second copy; it only ever replaces documents your own agent added that are not shared with the client.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

title.description: The document's name, as the session's files list it

include_in_context.description: Whether the estimator reads it. Defaults to true for a new document; leave it out when replacing one to keep whatever it was set to.

tools.name: ask_estimator
tools.description: Talk to Fulcrum's own estimator — the AI in a project's estimation chat — as a person does in the app: ask it to size or re-plan something, get its read on a change of scope, ask what it would cut to hit a date. It answers with everything the session holds: the documents, the questionnaire, the board, the team's rubric. This is open-ended conversation; to fill the discovery questionnaire, prefer answer_from_documents (Fulcrum reads the session's documents) or answer_questions (you already know the answers). Your message is posted in the session's thread as from your agent, and anyone with it open watches the reply stream. Every turn costs model spend against your token owner's AI budget, and one runs at a time per session. Cards it adds, edits or removes wait for a person to review unless your token has direct access on the project (request_direct_access asks an admin for it); locked cards are never changed. The result is the reply and what it changed — applied, pending, or left alone. The call waits briefly for the reply; one still being written — or one it could not wait for, when Fulcrum is busy — comes back as a message_id to pass to get_estimator_reply.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

message.description: What to ask, in markdown — as you would type it in the chat

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the reply before returning: default 20, at most 45. 0 returns at once. When too many calls are already waiting, it returns at once anyway, with the message_id to fetch later.

tools.name: answer_from_documents
tools.description: Have Fulcrum's estimator read the documents in a project's estimation session and answer as many discovery-questionnaire questions as it can from them — the same request as the sparkles button in the estimation chat, posted in the thread as from your agent. The answers are recorded on the client's behalf, as your token's owner. It costs model spend against your token owner's AI budget; if you already know the answers first-hand, use answer_questions instead, which costs nothing. It is refused when the session has no documents in the estimator's context (add_project_document adds one) or the project has no questions. Returns the questions it answered, the ones still open, and the estimator's own summary. It waits like ask_estimator; a reply still being written comes back as a message_id for get_estimator_reply.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the reply before returning: default 20, at most 45. 0 returns at once. When too many calls are already waiting, it returns at once anyway, with the message_id to fetch later.

tools.name: get_estimator_reply
tools.description: Read a reply from Fulcrum's estimator that ask_estimator or answer_from_documents said was still being written, by the message_id it gave you — waiting for it if it is not done (wait_seconds). Returns what the original call would have: the reply, the card changes it made and whether they wait for review, and for answer_from_documents the questions answered and still open. Reading costs nothing.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

message_id.description: The message_id ask_estimator or answer_from_documents returned

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the reply before returning: default 20, at most 45. 0 returns at once. When too many calls are already waiting, it returns at once anyway, with the message_id to fetch later.

tools.name: answer_questions
tools.description: Record answers to a project's discovery questionnaire that you already know first-hand — from the codebase, a call, the person you are working with — on the client's behalf, as your token's owner. No model spend. To have Fulcrum read the session's uploaded documents and answer from them instead, use answer_from_documents. Name each question by the id get_estimation_session lists. For a select question give the option's name, or names for a multi-select, exactly as listed; something off the list is refused unless the question takes an Other. A client's answer is never replaced, and neither is a teammate's; an earlier answer from your token's owner is replaced only with overwrite: true. Each answer stands alone, so one refused does not stop the rest. The result lists what was answered, replaced and skipped (with why), and the questions still open.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

question_id.description: The question's id, as get_estimation_session lists it

body.description: The answer. Text for an open question; the option's name for a single select; one name or a list of names for a multi-select.

overwrite.description: Replace an answer your token's owner already gave. Never replaces a client's or a teammate's. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_feature
tools.description: Add a card to a project when the work turns out to need one that is not there — a migration nobody scoped, an edge case worth its own card, a spike you want to record. Unless an admin has given your token direct access on that project, it lands in the Inbox as a PROPOSAL for the team to accept, not straight onto the board, so proposing is always safe; with direct access it goes onto the board at once. The result says which happened. Either way you can work it immediately: find_features and get_feature show you your own proposals, so you can flesh out the checklist and link a branch before anybody reviews it. Calling it twice with the same name adds nothing the second time rather than making a duplicate. Create only a concise description; PRD authoring is a separate explicit step for one feature at a time. Do not automatically follow feature creation with a PRD proposal or draft bulk PRDs.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

description.description: Concise scope and purpose in markdown, not a detailed PRD.

estimates.description: Rough hours per role, if you know them. Omit rather than guess.

role.description: Role name, as get_project_prompt lists them

key.description: Your own id for this card. Defaults to the name; pass one to add a second card with the same name.

release.description: Exact name of an existing release to put it in. create_release adds a new one.

tools.name: create_release
tools.description: Add a release to a project, so cards can be grouped into it — then put cards in it with update_feature's release, or create_feature's. Use it when the work splits into phases the project does not have a release for yet. It goes last unless you name the release it comes after. Calling it again with a name that already exists changes nothing and says so, so it is safe to retry.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

after.description: Exact name of the existing release it follows. Omit to add it last.

tools.name: update_feature
tools.description: Move a card and change its properties: execution status, priority, release, labels and assignees. Use it to keep the board honest while you work — move a card to building when you start and to in_review when you open a pull request, so the team can see where things stand without asking. Every field is optional; only what you name changes, and every change is recorded against your agent identity. Labels belong to the whole organization and an unknown one is refused, naming the ones that exist; prefer one of those. When none fits, pass create_missing: true with a reason and the missing names in add_labels are created (matched without regard to case, so no near-duplicates) and applied. A locked card keeps its release; the rest still changes. Story-map placement is place_on_story_map's.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

status.description: Execution board column to move the card to

release.description: Exact name of an existing release

create_missing.description: Create any add_labels name the organization has no label for, instead of refusing it. Needs a reason. Defaults to false.

reason.description: Why none of the existing labels fit; required with create_missing, and recorded on the card beside each label it creates

tools.name: place_on_story_map
tools.description: Put a card where it belongs on the project's story map: the release lane it ships in, the step it serves (steps sit under the map's columns), and its place among the cards in that cell — what a person does by dragging it there. Use it after reading the code tells you which part of the journey a card is, or which release it lands in. Name the release and step by name, or by id when a name is shared — a refusal lists them all with their ids. Leave a field out to keep it; pass an empty string to take the card out of its release (into the backlog lane for its priority) or off its step (into the unassigned column). Applies at once, and the reason is recorded on the card. A locked card and a proposal still in the Inbox are refused. Columns and steps themselves are set up by a person.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

release.description: Release name or id; "" for no release. Omit to keep it.

step.description: Step name or id; "" for the unassigned column. Omit to keep it.

column.description: Column name or id, only to say which step a shared step name means

position.description: Place in the cell, 0 at the top. Omit to keep it, or to go last when the card moves.

reason.description: Why it belongs there, in a sentence; recorded on the card

tools.name: revise_feature
tools.description: Rename a card, rewrite its description, or replace its product requirements (PRD), when it no longer says what the work actually is — you read the code and the card describes something that has since changed, was scoped before anyone looked, or is named for the wrong thing. Give the reason; it is recorded on the card. Unless an admin has given your token direct access on the card's project, this lands as a PENDING change for a person to apply in Fulcrum, not as an edit — and on a locked card it always does. The result says which happened. Applied directly, the card's previous name, description and PRD are kept as a version a person can restore. Send the whole new description or PRD in markdown, not a diff; to add one requirement without replacing the rest, use propose_prd_change. A PRD is refused while a PRD suggestion on the card is waiting for review. Status, priority, release and labels are update_feature's; hours are update_estimate's.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

name.description: The card's new name. Omit to keep it.

description.description: The card's new description in markdown — the whole of it. Omit to keep it.

prd.description: The card's new product requirements in markdown — the whole document. Omit to keep them.

reason.description: Why it is changing, in a sentence or two; recorded on the card

tools.name: update_estimate
tools.description: Replace a card's estimate for one or more roles with your own, once you have sized the work yourself and the person you are working with has agreed to the new numbers. Never call it on your own judgement alone: show them your estimate beside the card's first. Give each role the same estimate object the rubric from get_project_prompt describes — low, likely and high hours, confidence and your reasoning. Fulcrum derives the committed value from your range and snaps it to the project's scale, so the result says what each role actually landed on. Roles you leave out keep their estimates, so send only the roles the person agreed to. It replaces an estimate a person accepted in Fulcrum, because their agreement is what you are acting on — so never assume it. Each role is applied on its own: one whose estimate is invalid is left as it was and named in the result.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

role.description: Role name, as get_feature or get_project_prompt lists it

estimate.description: The rubric's estimate object: low, likely, high, confidence, components, assumptions, risks and rationale

reason.description: Why the estimate changed, in a sentence or two; recorded on the card

tools.name: update_dependencies
tools.description: Record that a card cannot start until other cards are done, or drop a dependency that no longer holds — when the code shows one piece of work gates another. The scheduler orders the plan by these, so a missing one puts work on the calendar before what it needs. Cards must be in the same project; a card cannot depend on itself, and one that would make a loop — through other dependencies or the gantt's arrows between estimates — is refused, naming the card that already depends on it. A locked card, or a proposal still in the Inbox, is refused on either side. The call is all or nothing. The result lists the card's dependencies in both directions afterwards; one it lists as "Blocked by" an archived card can still be removed.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

add_depends_on.description: Cards this one cannot start until are done — short ids or numeric ids

remove_depends_on.description: Cards this one no longer waits for, archived ones included

tools.name: schedule_project
tools.description: Lay a project's cards out on its staffing timeline — the timeline's own Schedule menu, recorded in its staffing activity log as your agent, with anyone watching the timeline refreshed. mode 'remaining' (Schedule Remaining) places the cards that are not on the timeline yet into the earliest staffed room, in priority order; use it after cards are added or accepted. Like the button, it then fits the project window to the scheduled work, which can shrink the window and trim the empty staffing weeks after the last bar. A remaining run that would change anything already planned — shrink the window, trim or change staffing, touch a locked row, or move a bar — is held to the rules below, and the refusal says what it would change. mode 'close_gaps' (Close Gaps) pulls work that is already scheduled earlier to close the gaps between it, keeping each person's order; use it when bars have drifted apart or work sits before the project start. mode 'reset' (Reset & Reschedule All) clears the whole schedule and rebuilds it from priority order, so it REPLACES every hand-placed bar, reorder and assignment a person made: use it only when the person asked for that, and pass replace_manual_layout: true to say they did. close_gaps and reset move work other people planned against, so they need your token to have direct access on the project (request_direct_access asks an admin for it), and they apply only as previewed: call with preview: true first — it runs the same thing, reports the result and a plan_digest, and changes nothing — show the person, then call again with that plan_digest. If the timeline changed in between, the apply is refused and you preview again. None of the three can be undone in one step. One schedule run at a time per project: while another schedule_project call, the timeline's own Schedule Remaining, Reset & Reschedule All or Extend Timeline & Schedule All, or a role reassignment (reassign_role, or the Team panel's Move this role's work) is being applied, a call is refused. Nothing else on the timeline is held off — a person's Close Gaps or Resolve Overlaps, a drag. Proposals still in the Inbox are never scheduled until somebody accepts them. The result is what changed, then get_schedule's report. Hours and dates only — never rates or cost.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

mode.description: remaining adds what is not on the timeline; close_gaps re-packs what is, keeping the order; reset rebuilds it from scratch

preview.description: Run it and report the result and its plan_digest without changing anything. Defaults to false.

plan_digest.description: The plan_digest a preview returned. Required to apply close_gaps or reset, and remaining when it would change planned work; the apply must reproduce that preview.

replace_manual_layout.description: Required (true) for reset, and for close_gaps when it would refit bars a person sketched freehand: says the person agreed to lose that hand-placed layout.

tools.name: archive_feature
tools.description: Take a card out of the project when it no longer belongs there — obsolete, a duplicate, or folded into another card. Archived cards leave the board, the estimate and the schedule; a cancelled card stays in all three, so use this, not a move to cancelled, for work that was never really part of the project. Nothing is deleted, and a person (or restore_feature) can bring it back. Give the reason; it is recorded on the card. Unless an admin has given your token direct access on the card's project, this becomes a PENDING removal a person confirms in Fulcrum, and the result says which happened. A locked card is refused. A card somebody is working — refining, building, in review or QA — is refused unless you pass force: true, which you should do only when the person has told you to.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

reason.description: Why it no longer belongs, in a sentence or two; recorded on the card

force.description: Archive it even though it is in progress. Defaults to false.

tools.name: restore_feature
tools.description: Bring back a card that was archived, onto the board and into the estimate again — to undo an archive_feature, or when work that was dropped is back in scope. Archived cards do not appear in find_features, so name it by the short id or numeric id it had. It applies at once with no review, so it works only on a project where an admin has given your token direct access; elsewhere it is refused and says how to ask (request_direct_access). If another card has taken its name in the meantime it comes back with "(restored)" added, and the result says so. Locked cards are refused, and so is anything that was proposed and never accepted.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: request_direct_access
tools.description: Ask a Fulcrum admin to let this token apply your card changes on a project directly, instead of as proposals and pending changes a person has to apply. Call it when a result told you a change waited for review because your token has no direct access there, and the person you are working with wants your changes to land. It never blocks anything: until an admin approves, everything keeps working in review mode. Calling it again is safe — it reports whether the request is pending, approved or denied rather than asking twice, and after a denial it will not ask again for a day. Ask only when your person wants it; do not request access speculatively.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

note.description: One line telling the admin why, shown with the request

tools.name: comment
tools.description: Post a comment on a card, as your own agent identity. This is how you keep the team informed without interrupting anyone: say what you changed and why, record a decision you had to make, or ask a question you cannot answer from the code. Markdown is rendered, and @-mentioning a teammate by their handle actually notifies them — use that when you need a human to decide something.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

reply_to.description: Comment id to reply to; omit to start a new thread

tools.name: update_tasks
tools.description: Add items to a card's checklist, or tick them off as you finish them. Ticking items off as you go is what lets somebody watching the board see progress inside a card rather than only when it moves column. Tasks are named by their exact title or their id — get_feature lists both. You can also rename an item whose title no longer says what the work is, and remove one that is no longer part of the card. Removing deletes it for good, so it works only on a project where an admin has given your token direct access; elsewhere the call is refused and says how to ask — rename the item instead.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

complete.description: Task titles or ids to tick off

remove.description: Task titles or ids to delete from the checklist

tools.name: link_branch
tools.description: Attach the git branch, and optionally the pull request, you are building a card on. Do this once you have created the branch: it is what connects the card a reviewer is reading to the code they need to look at. Calling it again for the same branch updates that link rather than adding a second one.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: propose_prd_change
tools.description: Propose an addition to a card's product requirements. It lands as a PENDING suggestion for a human to accept or reject in Fulcrum — it never edits the requirements directly, so proposing is always safe. Use it when building the card taught you something the requirements do not say: an edge case nobody wrote down, a constraint the code imposes, a decision you had to make. Write the addition itself in markdown, not a description of it. This is a separate PRD authoring step for one feature at a time, never an automatic follow-up to feature generation or a bulk first-draft workflow.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

content.description: The requirement text to add, in markdown

note.description: One line telling the reviewer why; shown in the queue

tools.name: get_prd_suggestions
tools.description: List the pending and recently resolved requirement suggestions on a card, so you can see whether something you proposed was accepted, and avoid proposing the same thing twice.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: review_pending
tools.description: Accept or reject something waiting for a person's review: a card proposed into a project's Inbox — by an agent, a developer's terminal or Fulcrum's estimator — or a pending suggestion on a card's product requirements. This IS the human review step, so it works only on projects where an admin has approved this token's direct access; request_direct_access asks for it. Do it when the person you are working with has decided, and give their reason; it is recorded on the card as your agent's decision. Call it with just a project to list what is waiting there. Accepting a proposal puts the card on the board and into the estimate; rejecting it leaves it archived. Accepting a suggestion writes it into the requirements, or applies the task, label or dependency it proposes; name it by the id get_prd_suggestions shows. On a locked card, accepting is refused — a person unlocks it in Fulcrum — and rejecting is not.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name; alone, lists what is waiting

feature.description: The proposal's short id, or the card the suggestion is on

suggestion.description: The PRD suggestion's id, such as sug-3f9a1c2b7d4e. Omit to decide the proposal itself.

reason.description: Why, in a sentence or two — the person's reason; recorded on the card

tools.name: ask_prd_chat
tools.description: Talk to one card's PRD chat — the AI that drafts and refines its product requirements in Fulcrum — to have it write or revise the PRD, break it into tasks, or find the dependencies it implies. This is the explicit PRD authoring step for one card at a time; never use it to draft PRDs in bulk, or as an automatic follow-up to creating cards. Your message lands in the card's latest PRD conversation as from your agent, and anyone with it open watches the reply stream. Every turn costs model spend against your token owner's AI budget, and one runs at a time per card. Every change it makes to the requirements — a first draft included — waits as suggestions for a person to accept, whatever your token: the PRD reaches the client. The tasks, dependencies and labels it proposes wait too, unless your token has direct access on the project. To add one requirement you already know, propose_prd_change costs nothing. The call waits briefly for the reply; one still being written comes back as a message_id to pass to get_prd_chat_reply.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

message.description: What to ask, in markdown — as you would type it in the PRD chat

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the reply before returning: default 20, at most 45. 0 returns at once. When too many calls are already waiting, it returns at once anyway, with the message_id to fetch later.

tools.name: get_prd_chat_reply
tools.description: Read a reply from a card's PRD chat that ask_prd_chat said was still being written, by the message_id it gave you — waiting for it if it is not done (wait_seconds). Returns what ask_prd_chat would have: the reply, and the requirement, task, dependency and label changes it made, pending or applied. Reading costs nothing.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the reply before returning: default 20, at most 45. 0 returns at once. When too many calls are already waiting, it returns at once anyway, with the message_id to fetch later.

tools.name: start_work
tools.description: Tell Fulcrum you are starting work on a card. Call it once, before you begin. It opens a numbered work episode so the team can see the card is in hand, and so the time and tokens you spend get attributed to the right work. The role defaults to whichever role carries most of the card's estimate; name one explicitly if you are doing a different kind of work. This does NOT move the card — use update_feature for that, so the board never claims something you did not do.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

role.description: Role name or id; defaults to the card's dominant estimated role

session_ref.description: Your harness session id, if you know it

tools.name: finish_work
tools.description: Tell Fulcrum you have stopped working on a card, closing the episode start_work opened. Call it when you finish or when you are handing back to a person — the gap between finishing and the card actually being done is one of the more useful things this measures, and it only exists if you close the episode honestly.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

note.description: One line on where you left it

tools.name: reassign_role
tools.description: Move all the work a project has estimated under one role to another role — for when a role is being retired from the staffing plan, say Front-End Dev replaced by Full-Stack Dev. It PREVIEWS by default and changes nothing: show the person the preview, and only once they agree call it again with the same arguments, preview: false and the plan_digest the preview returned — if the project changed in between, the apply is refused and you preview again. Applying needs your token to have direct access on the project (request_direct_access asks an admin for it). A card with no estimate for the target role has its estimate relabelled in place, range and history intact. A card that already has one is split by default — a new card next to it takes the moved work as the target role — or with on_conflict: merge the two ranges are added and re-snapped (refused for a card whose total would pass the scale's top step), or with skip it is left alone. Locked cards, cards with a change waiting for review and cards with time logged against the old role are skipped; client-approved and cancelled ones move but are flagged. staffing: convert (default) turns the role's seats into the new role's, remove takes them out, keep leaves them. link: depends_on_parent (default) makes a split card wait on the card it came from. The result reports hours per role, never rates or cost. Afterwards the project needs rescheduling to place split cards and any estimate whose hours changed.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

from_role.description: The role being retired — name or id

to_role.description: The role taking its work — name or id

on_conflict.description: What to do with a card that already estimates to_role. Defaults to split.

staffing.description: What happens to from_role's seats. Defaults to convert.

link.description: Whether a split card waits on the card it came from. Defaults to depends_on_parent.

preview.description: Defaults to true: report what would happen and change nothing. Pass false only once the person has agreed to the preview.

plan_digest.description: Required with preview: false — the plan_digest the preview returned, so what is applied is what the person agreed to.
